subject: Platinum
hook: PLATINUM IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Far from being scattered across the globe like other precious metals, roughly 75% of the world's known platinum is concentrated in a single geological layer in South Africa called the Merensky Reef, which accounts for over 70% of global mine production.
angle_support: The specific layer he found, named the Merensky Reef, contains around 75 % of the world's known platinum.
In 2025, South Africa was the top producer of platinum, with an estimated 120,000 kg, about 71 % of world mine production of 170,000 kg (370,000 lb)
title: The Single Reef That Holds Most of the World’s Platinum
description: Most people think platinum is spread across many mines, but a single layer in South Africa provides the majority of the metal. The Merensky Reef alone supplies over 70 % of global production.
narration: PLATINUM IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You assume platinum is scattered in mines worldwide like gold or silver. In reality, most of it comes from one narrow geological layer in South Africa today. Geologist Hans Merensky identified the Merensky Reef in 1924; today that single stratum holds roughly 75 % of known platinum and supplies over 70 % of global mine output each year from South Africa's Bushveld Igneous Complex region and remains the cornerstone of the industry. All that glitters now traces back to one South African seam.
